name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: I’ll draft the first PACKAGE now: `excv_pkg_core` in `./packages/excav_core/` with a `mod.rs`, `lib.rs`, and `Cargo.toml` labeled “Created by EXCAVA”. I’ll seed it with a `TabEnrich` trait and a `tes!` macro stub. After that, I’ll run `cargo test --package excv_pkg_core` to confirm the artifact exists and the lead can decide.

name: Vet
text: Vet — the skeptic — leans forward: *"Hold. You’re rushing the `TabEnrich` trait into `excv_pkg_core` before the team’s even agreed on the tab system’s architecture—what if the trait’s design forces downstream packages into a brittle coupling? Where’s the evidence that this abstraction won’t collapse under real-world tab variants? Also, your `tes!` macro stub is a placeholder—how do you verify its *existence* meets the done-criteria without a concrete test case?"*

name: Forge
text:
Forge: I’ll isolate the tab system’s contract first—create `./packages/excav_core/src/tab/mod.rs` and `./packages/excav_core/src/tab/traits.rs`, each stamped “Created by EXCAVA”. I’ll draft only the `TabEnrich` trait skeleton (no impls) and a `tes!` macro stub that panics on use, then run `cargo test --package excv_pkg_core` to confirm the artifact exists and fails cleanly. This gives Vet a concrete artifact to critique without forcing downstream coupling.

name: Vet
text: Vet: *"Still too fast. You’re proposing a `TabEnrich` trait skeleton with no impls, but where’s the proof it’s even necessary? A trait without consumers is just speculative coupling—what if the tab system’s real needs emerge from downstream packages first? Show me the RFC or at least a mock consumer package that *demands* this abstraction, or you’re building a solution in search of a problem."*
